long_biography.plain_text:
Adler's transformation began when Paolo Scudieri entered the company in the early 1980s and looked beyond its existing polyurethane applications. He presented the material to carmakers and patented the lightweight Fonocel sound-insulation system, helping move the family manufacturer towards higher-value automotive components. The company expanded from southern Italy into Europe and South America as those applications gained scale.

A decisive step came with Adler's acquisition of Germany's HP Pelzer, begun in 2010 and completed later in the decade. Combining the businesses created Adler Pelzer Group, an international supplier of acoustic and thermal systems for vehicles. Scudieri remains chairman and controlling shareholder, preserving family control while directing the acquisition-led expansion that made the inherited platform a global automotive group.

Paolo's new automotive applications, Fonocel patent, international expansion and HP Pelzer acquisition demonstrate material personal growth, supporting Inherited and expanded. Adler sources variously describe entry into HP Pelzer in 2010, initial majority ownership in 2011, full ownership in 2013 and completion of the wider integration in 2016. The biographies therefore describe the acquisition as beginning in 2010 and completing later in the decade rather than forcing a single closing date.
